definition: A graph-structured representation of knowledge consisting of entities (nodes) and their relationships (edges), used to organize and query structured information.
details: Knowledge graphs are used both as a data source for retrieval-augmented systems (as in GraphRAG) and as a target for information extraction tasks, where a model extracts entities and relations from unstructured text.
story: Think of a historian sorting through boxes of letters, building a picture of an era one sentence at a time. Boil it down and it is this: A graph-structured representation of knowledge consisting of entities (nodes) and their relationships (edges), used to organize and query structured information. Here is why it matters: Knowledge graphs are used both as a data source for retrieval-augmented systems (as in GraphRAG) and as a target for information extraction tasks, where a model extracts entities and relations from unstructured text. The words a model reads become the world it believes in. That care with the raw material is Knowledge Graph.
